producedBy.what: One page, put through the GetLoopLoop Vectorscope's fetch, extract and chunk steps locally, with the product's 26-passage cap, and no embedding step. Grouped by the agent's reading, not by embeddings; groups are a judgement, chunking and the 26-passage cap are the product's exact rules.

howToRead.grouping: Grouped by the agent's reading, not by embeddings; groups are a judgement, chunking and the 26-passage cap are the product's exact rules. The product groups passages by average-link clustering over embedding similarity; here the passages were read and grouped by subject instead, so two runs can group the same page differently. For the embedding-based reading with the map, run the page at https://www.getlooploop.com/vectorscope.
howToRead.unitOfAnalysis: A chunk is one passage as the pipeline split it — roughly 2000 characters, following the page's own headings where it has them. Chunks overlap by about 200 characters, so their lengths sum to more than the page.
howToRead.textHead: Only the first 240 characters of each chunk are included. Across this page that is 3979 of 14109 indexed characters, about 28%, and always the opening of each passage rather than a sample spread through it.
howToRead.keywords: Counted over the page's whole text, not the excerpts below. A term is one word or two: a two-word term is a pair the page writes side by side often enough that the pair is what it is saying, and where it is counted neither of its words is counted separately, so the occurrences still add up to the page. `count` is occurrences; `groups` is how many of the page's groups the term reaches, and `scope` is true when it reaches most of them. A term with `scope` true describes the page; one with it false is a single section's vocabulary — useful, but not a summary. Plurals were folded into the singular where the page uses both. The group counts rest on the grouping above, which is a judgement.
howToRead.agentLabel: v2: the name the agent gave the group after reading it, or null. It is a judgement, like the grouping; `label` and `labelSource` are the computed label as in v1.
howToRead.groupLabels: `labelSource` says where each name came from. "heading" is the page's own section heading and can be quoted. "keywords" is a computed guess — the group's most distinctive words — and is a hint, not a topic; do not quote it back as what the section is called.
howToRead.cohesion: null: cohesion is the mean cosine between a group's passage embeddings, and no embeddings were computed.
howToRead.selfSimilarity: null: the median cosine between passages needs embeddings, and none were computed.
howToRead.groupFloor: null: there was no similarity cut; the groups are a reading of the passages.
howToRead.duplicateOf: The index of an earlier, non-adjacent chunk this one repeats nearly word for word, as judged by reading — the product judges it from embeddings at cosine 0.94. The chunker's own overlap between neighbours is excluded.
howToRead.projectionExplained: null: there is no projection without vectors.
howToRead.whatCapReachedMeans: The pipeline indexes at most 26 chunks per page. `capReached` true with `charsUnread` above zero means an assistant reading this page never sees that tail.
howToRead.noindex: True when the page asks search engines not to index it. Says nothing about whether an assistant can read it, but it is often unintentional.

cannotAnswer: Sentiment or tone of the page. Only about 28% of the text is here, taken from the opening of each passage — enough to produce a confident-sounding verdict from an unrepresentative sample. If asked, say what the sample supports and that it is a sample.
Anything about competitors, or how this page compares to another. One page was read; no other page was fetched.
Which search or assistant prompts this page ranks or gets cited for. That needs a query inventory and measurement over time, neither of which is in this export.
Whether the page is factually correct, current, or original. Nothing here checked any claim on it.
How the page renders for a browser running JavaScript. This is a plain fetch, which is also what an assistant that does not run JavaScript sees.

How close any two passages are in an embedding space, or whether any assistant has indexed this page. No embeddings were computed, and this is a preview of the machine's view, not a guarantee of what any assistant does with it.
suggestedPrompt: This is a retrieval read-out of one web page. Using it, tell me: (1) what this page is about — lean on `keywords` where `describesWholePage` is true, since those are counted over the full text rather than the excerpts — group by group, naming groups only where labelSource is "heading"; (2) what someone asking an assistant about this subject would find here, and what they would not; (3) what to change first, ordered by how much it would change what an assistant retrieves — cite the chunk indexes or group ids your answer rests on. Where the payload's cannotAnswer list says the data does not support a claim, say so instead of estimating.

plan.problem: The empty result widget is inside main, so its step labels and counter captions become passage #1: a retriever stores "1. Fetched 2. Extracted …" as content.
plan.fix: Render the result widget only after a run, or mark the placeholder aria-hidden and move it out of main. If the counts should stay readable, say them in one sentence.
plan.before:
passages read
slots used of the 26-passage cap
characters the cap cut off (0 when the page fits)
plan.after: For each page, Vectorscope reports three counts: the passages it read, the slots used of its 26-passage cap, and the characters the cap cut off.

plan.problem: "How to read your result" is 2,450 characters under one h2, so the 2,000-character window cuts it and passage #6 opens with "to quote." mid-sentence.
plan.fix: Make each of the four readings its own h2 ("Chunks that never reach the index", "The extraction ratio", …), so every passage starts where its topic starts and carries the heading that names it.
plan.before: to quote. The passage a question actually retrieves Asking the page a question returns the passages that answer it, ranked, using only that page
plan.after: Which passage does a question retrieve? Asking Vectorscope a question returns the passages of the page that answer it, ranked, using only that page.

plan.problem: The FAQ is one h2 of 2,292 characters; the window splits the answer to "Is it really free?" across two passages, and #14 opens with "after the reading is produced".
plan.fix: Split the FAQ into two h2 sections (AI citations; using Vectorscope), each under 2,000 characters, so no answer is cut away from its question.
plan.before: after the reading is produced. No account is needed, so there is nothing to attach it to.
plan.after: Vectorscope does not keep the fetched page once the reading is produced, and it needs no account, so nothing is attached to you.

plan.before: Move it earlier on the page, or split the page so that passage has a budget of its own.
plan.after: If an important passage falls outside Vectorscope's 26-passage cap, move it earlier on the page, or split the page so that passage has a budget of its own.

plan.fix: Name the product and the limit in the first sentence.

facts.fact: A page contributes at most 26 passages; the rest is never read.
Long sections are cut into 2,000-character windows with 200 characters of overlap.
Only an h2 starts a passage; an h3 stays inside the passage of the h2 above it.
The grouping embeds each passage after the cut; the cut itself is not semantic.
A test of one URL takes about twenty seconds.
Free with a rate limit, no account; the fetched page is not retained.
